subject.title: [Bug]: Terminal provider model_not_available in subagent announce path can trigger chat.history storm and gateway event-loop starvation

question: Should this issue be solved as a narrow runtime containment fix, or should it become a broader provider/config/gateway recovery design item?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested fixes cross provider error semantics, subagent delivery guarantees, config hot-reload validation, and gateway liveness recovery; automation should not choose that product boundary alone.

options.title: Contain runtime failure first
options.body: Classify the terminal provider wording, prevent announce/history amplification, and wake or mark the parent with a bounded failure while leaving config validation and watchdog work to linked follow-ups.

options.title: Broaden into reliability design
options.body: Treat this as a larger provider/config/gateway recovery program and keep implementation paused until maintainers choose the combined behavior and proof bar.

options.title: Defer to related issues only
options.body: Close or deprioritize this only if maintainers decide the remaining provider-triggered announce storm is already covered by adjacent issues despite the current source gap.

recommendation.title: Contain runtime failure first
recommendation.body: Classify the terminal provider wording, prevent announce/history amplification, and wake or mark the parent with a bounded failure while leaving config validation and watchdog work to linked follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: The most direct current-source and history trail for both model classification and subagent lifecycle paths points to steipete, with Vincent Koc as a strong adjacent reviewer.
